_doc: Master target list for OpenTopography ingestion. Each entry is one region with bbox, dataset, tier, and fantasy-style hints. bulk_pull.py walks this. Tiers: 'showcase' (USGS 1m via OT+, single-bbox), 'stitched' (multi-tile composites for huge regions, use tile_stitch.py), 'premium' (30m large bbox), 'standard' (30m medium bbox), 'bathymetric' (GEBCO seafloor), 'highres_open' (LINZ/Arctic/REMA — endpoint TBD), 'mystery' (procedural unknowns). Storage budget ~50GB.

stitched._note: Regions too large for a single API call — use tile_stitch.py to fetch N×M tiles and seamlessly compose. Common case: full national-park-scale regions at 1m LiDAR, where each ~12km×12km tile fits the 250km² USGS1m limit. The stitched output goes into pipelines/terrain/output/<id>/height_16.png like any other DEM.

highres_open._note: 1m / 10m datasets that DO NOT require Pro tier. Pull-via-API is currently BLOCKED for LINZ1m / ArcticDEM / REMA — they're in the catalog, no Pro requirement, but the /globaldem endpoint rejects them (400). Endpoint is TBD; for now use catalog_search.py to confirm availability and download manually via OT's data-catalog UI. USGS10m DOES work via /usgsdem and is the immediately-usable high-res option for US locations.
